THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. All three go through a Read
that has TWO ceilings: it TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB. BOTH HAVE
ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE. iter127 hit the byte ceiling - the Read was refused, 459 KB, because the
`done` log had reached 397 KB of it. iter128 found the TOKEN cap had been truncating for longer and
unnoticed: at 74,115 bytes / 31,303 tokens, step 1 returned lines 1-43 of 92 and dropped `decisions`
(the six outstanding decisions), `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`.

CORRECTED AT ITER129, because a later method depends on it: TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT. The tool prints
"[Truncated: PARTIAL view - showing lines 1-462 of 1500 total (68900 tokens, cap 25000)]". iter128
called truncation "the worse failure because it looks like success"; the real risk is an agent
SKIMMING PAST an explicit notice, not the tool hiding anything. That notice is also the ONLY tokenizer
on this machine (no tiktoken, no anthropic, no transformers), and it is how iter129 calibrated the
size checker: build a file over the cap but under 256 KB, Read it whole, divide bytes by the reported
total. Markdown measured 2.604 B/tok, this file's JSON 2.368.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO PLAN.md.
It measures ALL THREE step-1 files (iter128's version measured only this one), prints each file's
HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates, distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields,
flags every other tools/loop file, and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting.
WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a
short pointer behind. There are SEVEN precedents - `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`,
`methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`, `spikesArchive`, and `decisions._archive` (iter130, the one that
keeps its pointer INSIDE the field it drained rather than as a sibling key) - and each one asserted
its round-trip before this file was rewritten. Do not discard content to make the check pass. WHEN IT TRIPS ON GATES.md OR
PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled section, never drop
one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.
phase:
M6 feature-complete. NO GATE IS TICKED AND decisions.formatOnEditHook IS STILL UNANSWERED, SO THERE IS STILL NO FEATURE WORK THE LOOP MAY DO. iter136, like 126-135, spent its increment on the loop's own machinery.

  THE FINDING: **THE ARCHIVE'S OWN LOOKUP INSTRUCTION WAS WRONG FOR 27 OF 135 ITERATIONS, AND ITS FAILURE MODE LOOKS LIKE A HIT.** `grep -n 'iterNNN' done-archive.jsonl`, the command `howToRead` prescribed, finds NOTHING for 3 iterations (object-shaped entries spell it `"iteration": NNN`) and, for 24 more, returns ONLY lines belonging to some OTHER entry — ask for iter113 and it hands back iter134's and iter135's records, which cite it in prose. 65 of 135 iterations get a match that is not their own. The archive is the loop's authoritative history and iter127's repair depended on reading it.

  LEAD (iv) RESOLVED AND THE ANSWER IS REASSURING: **no record was ever lost** — all 135 iterations are present, 107 as strings and 29 as objects. `n` is a LINE INDEX, +1 off the iteration number since line 50 because iter48 logged twice.

  FIXED in check-state-size.py (the script already required after every state.json edit): attribution, coverage and head checks, plus a working `--find <n>`. Proven 6/6 by mutation, including two cases that leave every pre-iter136 check green and one control that must stay green. Suite: 1375/1375, 0 skipped.
nextAction:
**RUN `dotnet build` AND `dotnet test` BEFORE YOU CHANGE ANYTHING, AND AGAIN AFTER YOUR LAST WRITE.** iter132 found the suite red at HEAD with two commits on top of it. Several tests sweep the tree's own prose (RepositorySlugTests over *.md/*.yml/*.json outside `tests/` and `tools/`, QuickstartTests over fenced commands), so a docs-only edit — GATES.md included — can turn it red. iter136 opened and closed green at 1375/1375, 0 skipped.

**CHECK GATES.md FIRST. FIVE MILESTONE GATES ARE OPEN AND ALL FIVE ARE MIRKO'S**, plus FOUR side items (paste-rule-8-2a, paste-force-push-hook, settings-corrections, paste-format-on-edit-hook). One line each in `gates`; full instructions in GATES.md. A ticked box is the only thing that turns this loop back into a working loop. Cheapest first: gate-m3 (add one `approved` label), gate-m4 (write one wrong comment), gate-m5 (answer decisions.m5Acceptance), gate-m2 (walk the 44 pages), gate-m6 (push main, then tag v0.1.0).

**GATE-M6 KEEPS GETTING SAFER.** iter134: ci.yml's Test step would have FAILED on the first push to main (Spectre's CI colour), fixed and re-proven 12/12 on full and `--depth 1` clones. iter135: that same job never exercised the mermaid renderer; now it does, 1375/1375 with nothing skipped. Both probes re-runnable in ~90 s and BOTH REPRODUCE A RUNNER RATHER THAN A LAPTOP: .mtk/paths-134/probe-ci-clean-clone.py, .mtk/paths-135/probe-ci-renderer-coverage.py. Re-run them before any future claim about CI.

**IF ANY SIDE ITEM IS TICKED OR decisions.formatOnEditHook IS SET:** GATES.md carries the exact follow-up for each, and the loop's half is the same shape every time — the paste lands in a file the loop cannot write, so `git add` it (iter89 committed `.claude/references/` that way), then re-run that item's probe as the in-situ confirmation: paste-format-on-edit-hook -> .mtk/paths-133/probe-project-settings-hook.py (expect the 127 gone); paste-force-push-hook -> `git push deny-probe-nonexistent-remote HEAD --force`, which cannot reach a real remote, and expect the hook's §8.2 refusal. For formatOnEditHook "delete", the `hooks` key comes out and tools/hooks/format-on-edit.py is deleted with it.

**IF NOTHING IS TICKED:** re-run the two liveness probes (~10 s each: `python3 .mtk/paths-121/probe-labels.py`, `python3 .mtk/paths-113/verify-space.py`), then end WAITING-GATE. That is the honest ending. iters 126-136 all took it and EVERY ITERATION WILL UNTIL A BOX IS TICKED. Do not invent work to avoid it.

**READ tools/loop/method-notes.md BEFORE WRITING A PROBE OR A TEST**, and **USE `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py --find <n>` TO READ AN ITERATION OUT OF THE ARCHIVE** — a bare grep is wrong for 27 of them and its wrong answers look like right ones (iter136). THIS FILE'S BUDGET HEADROOM is in method-notes too, and it is TIGHT: ~19.0k of a 20k-token budget.

**THE CLASS OF WORK THAT IS STILL LEGITIMATE WHEN THE FEATURE BACKLOG IS EMPTY: run the protocol literally and report what does not work.** 126-133: the dead phone-push channel, the two step-1 Read ceilings, the checker measuring one of three files, §8.2 covering one spelling of force-push, the unread CLI stderr, the red suite at HEAD, the dead format-on-edit hook, the archive missing iter132. 134: ci.yml red on the runner it had never run on. 135: that runner never installing the renderer. 136: the archive's own lookup instruction. THE BOUNDARY, and hold it: this licence covers the loop's own machinery — the files the protocol reads, the channels it claims, the checks and guards it relies on. It does NOT license inventing feature work or a sixth PLAN.md sweep.

**LEADS OF THAT CLASS STILL UNEXERCISED.** Spent and closed, do not redo: the [ENFORCED] audit, the step-1 read ceilings, the `--resume` path, the MODEL mechanism, the project-settings hook question, (ii) at iter134, (vi) at iter135, and (iv)+(v) at iter136 — **(iv) closed with 'nothing was lost': all 135 iterations are archived.** STILL UNTOUCHED, and it is the last one on the list: **(iii) THE DRIVER'S ITERATION NUMBER IS NOT state.json's.** `loop.log` said 'Iteration 157' while this file said 131, because the driver's counter resets on every restart while this one only ever increments, so every 'iterNNN' mis-maps to its log file by ~26. The one-line fix is in tools/loop/docume-loop.sh, which scratchInventory says is NOT the loop's to commit, so it is a paste-shaped ask rather than an edit. NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: iter136 found a SECOND numbering offset — archive `n` runs +1 ahead of the iteration number since line 50 — so there are two independent off-by-somes in play; do not conflate them.
blockers: OPEN, ITER121, PHRASED AS A QUESTION — **may the loop push to origin/main?** WHAT I NEED: a value in `tools/loop/state.json → decisions.pushPolicy` — "always", "on-request" or "never". WHAT THE FACT IS: origin/main is at 699c855 ("iter74"); local main is at iter120; `git status -sb` reads [ahead 93] against a remote ref fetched the same day. The loop has never pushed in 120 iterations and no earlier iteration recorded it. Nothing is lost — every commit is on this machine. WHY I DID NOT JUST DO IT: 93 commits landing on Moberg's org fires ci.yml (push to main), is outward-facing, and is unfixable without the history rewrite §8.2 forbids; no gate or protocol line authorises it. WHAT I DO ONCE IT IS SET: "always" — push at the end of each iteration that commits, starting with the 93; "on-request" — push only when a gate needs the remote and say so; "never" — stop raising it, and gate-m6 keeps its 'push main by hand before you tag' step. THIS IS NOT BLOCKING ANY OFFLINE WORK; it blocks the remote-dependent half of gate-m5-refresh-roundtrip and makes gate-m6's tag step misleading if unanswered. AS OF ITER128 THE COUNT IS [ahead 104], not the 93 recorded above; the question and every consequence are otherwise unchanged.

OPEN, ITER75, PHRASED AS A QUESTION — **may the §8.2a rule amendment be pasted?** NON-FATAL: it blocks no milestone work, nothing in the build waits on it, and it needs no follow-up once done. WHAT I NEED: the bullet in tools/loop/rule-8-2a-paste.md (everything below the `---`, verbatim, no drafting) added to .claude/rules/git-workflow.md directly beneath §8.2, with §8.2 itself left untouched. WHY IT EXISTS: you authorized release.yml to force-move the composite action's floating `v1` tag (decisions.compositeAction: "floating-v1", built at db240dc), but §8.2 still reads "NEVER force-push or rewrite history" with no exception, so a future iteration could read it, call that step a violation, and delete work you asked for. The amendment scopes the exception to that one tag, on the runner, and restates that branch history stays untouchable. WHY THE LOOP WILL NOT DO IT, and why no iteration should try again: Edit AND Write refuse `.claude/**` (iter75 proved the allowlist entries added at 6db1c39 do not reach it; an interactive session was refused the same edit). An allowlisted python3 WOULD work and is deliberately not used — the content is an agent-facing rule that WIDENS force-push authority, and the guard in the way exists to stop an agent installing exactly that. FULL REASONING: GATES.md -> paste-rule-8-2a, which step 1 reads anyway. If you would rather the rule stayed unwritten, say so here and I will stop carrying the ask.

OPEN, ITER130, PHRASED AS A QUESTION — **may the force-push guard be installed?** It is one paste and the loop cannot do it. WHAT I NEED: the single fenced `json` block in tools/loop/loop-settings-paste.md pasted over the whole of tools/loop/loop-settings.json. WHERE: that file; it is a whole-file replacement, not an insertion. WHAT THE FACT IS: rule §8.2 is labelled "[ENFORCED — loop-settings deny + protocol]" and the deny half only covers the flag-first spelling. Measured at iter130 against a remote name that does not exist, so no probe could push: `git push --force <remote> HEAD` DENIED, but `git push <remote> HEAD --force`, `git push <remote> HEAD -f` and `git push --force-with-lease <remote> HEAD` were ALL ALLOWED, because the patterns match whole tokens from the START of the command. With `origin main` in place of that remote the second of those rewrites origin/main, which §8.2 says never happens and cannot be undone. No deny list closes it (a remote and a refspec of any name sit before the flag), so the fix is a PreToolUse hook: tools/loop/hooks/deny-history-rewrite.py, committed, inert until wired, proven both directions 25/25 by .mtk/paths-130/mutate-force-push-guard.py. **PROVEN END-TO-END AT ITER131, BEFORE YOU INSTALL IT.** iter130 could not answer whether a hook in a --settings file loads and fires at all, and left that to the iteration after the paste. It did not need the paste: .mtk/paths-131/probe-hook-from-settings.py hands the exact block to a child `claude -p` as a throwaway scratch settings file and scores 3/3 — the hook REFUSED `git push deny-probe-nonexistent-remote HEAD --force` with the §8.2 message; the same command under today's live settings REACHED GIT, reproducing the hole; and `git status --short` under the paste RAN CLEAN, so it is selective rather than a blanket block. Hooks are honoured from --settings, and an untrusted workspace does not stop them. Nothing was installed to learn this. WHY I STILL DO NOT DO IT MYSELF: Edit on tools/loop/loop-settings.json is REFUSED under acceptEdits (a Write of a new file under tools/loop/hooks/ succeeded in the same session, so the guard is specific to the settings file). An allowlisted python3 WOULD work and is DELIBERATELY NOT USED, on the paste-rule-8-2a precedent: this change only NARROWS authority, but anything that can add a PreToolUse hook to its own settings can also add one that auto-approves, and that is precisely what the guard in the way exists to stop. .mtk/paths-130/validate-settings-paste.py proves the block adds no allow entry, drops none, keeps every deny and wires the hook (45 allow / 9 deny vs live 45 / 6). WHAT I DO ONCE IT IS PASTED: run that same command against the LIVE file as the in-situ confirmation and record it. NOT BLOCKING ANY MILESTONE WORK: nothing in the build waits on it, and what stands in the hole meanwhile is that the loop has never pushed in 131 iterations. IF YOU WOULD RATHER IT STAYED UNWIRED, say so here and I will stop carrying the ask. RELATED: same class as paste-rule-8-2a, and it interacts with decisions.pushPolicy — the day the loop may push is the day this hole stops being theoretical.

OPEN, ITER131, TWO QUESTIONS, NEITHER BLOCKING ANYTHING — **two one-line settings corrections that are yours to make.** Both found by reading the CLI's own stderr, which docume-loop.sh has captured into every iteration log via 2>&1 for 130 iterations while nothing read it. (a) MAY THIS WORKSPACE BE TRUSTED? WHAT I NEED: `projects["/Users/mirkobudimir/Dev/docu-me"].hasTrustDialogAccepted` = `true` in ~/.claude.json, or run Claude Code interactively here once and accept the dialog. IT IS `false`, so every iteration the CLI ignores three `.claude/settings.json` allow entries — `Bash(dotnet build:*)`, `Bash(dotnet test:*)`, `Bash(dotnet format:*)`, the protocol's own verification commands. COSTS NOTHING TODAY, which is why nobody noticed: loop-settings.json's broader `Bash(dotnet:*)` comes through --settings and IS honoured. ONCE SET: `.claude/settings.json`'s allow half stops being inert, so anything added there later actually applies. (b) DO YOU WANT YOUR GLOBAL `.env` WRITE-DENIES TO WORK? WHAT I NEED: in ~/.claude/settings.json, `Write(.env)` -> `Edit(.env)` and `Write(.env.*)` -> `Edit(.env.*)`. The CLI reports that `Write(path)` rules are not matched by file permission checks — only `Edit(path)` is — so as spelled those two denies enforce NOTHING. Related to rules §0.3/§1.1, hence surfacing it. WHY NOT ME: (a) is your global state outside this repo and trusting a workspace is a security decision; (b) lives under `.claude/`, refused to the loop, and an allowlisted python3 could route around that and must not. **AND ONE THING THE LOOP WILL NOT DO EVEN IF ASKED:** the same diagnostic names `Write(.claude/**)` in tools/loop/loop-settings.json, and the CLI's suggested `Edit(.claude/**)` is exactly the rewrite that would give the loop write access to its own rules — dead as written is the CORRECT state there. FULL DETAIL: GATES.md -> settings-corrections. Want either ask dropped? Say so here.

OPEN, ITER133, PHRASED AS A QUESTION — **may the format-on-edit hook be fixed, or should it be deleted?** ONE PASTE, NOTHING WAITS ON IT. WHAT I NEED, either one: the single fenced `json` block in tools/loop/claude-settings-paste.md pasted over the whole of `.claude/settings.json`, OR the word "delete" in `decisions.formatOnEditHook`. WHAT THE FACT IS: that file has declared a PostToolUse format-on-edit hook since the 2026-07-24 bootstrap and it has FIRED AND FAILED on every Edit and Write since — `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is empty in a project settings file (the CLI sets it only for plugin-supplied hooks), so the command runs `bash "/hooks/format-on-edit.sh"` and exits 127, and that script was never generated. It went unnoticed for 133 iterations because A FAILING PostToolUse HOOK IS INVISIBLE TO THE AGENT: exit_code=127, outcome='error', 0 mentions in any user/assistant turn, result.is_error False. ALREADY BUILT AND PROVEN, so this is a tested change and not a draft: tools/hooks/format-on-edit.py committed and 5/5, the paste validated 12/12 (permissions byte-identical, nothing granted), and the block proven end to end 3/3 in a child session against a control cell. THE PART THAT IS GENUINELY YOURS IS COST: ~7.0 s per .cs edit, 0 for everything else. WHAT I DO ONCE ANSWERED: "fix" — commit the pasted file (`git add` is not blocked) and re-run .mtk/paths-133/probe-project-settings-hook.py as in-situ confirmation; "delete" — ship the hook-key removal the same way and delete the script. WHY NOT ME: `.claude/` is refused to the loop and an allowlisted python3 must not route around it for the file that governs the loop's own behaviour. NOT BLOCKING ANY MILESTONE WORK. FULL DETAIL, INCLUDING THE MEASUREMENT TABLE: GATES.md → paste-format-on-edit-hook.

gates.authoritative: GATES.md. It is richer than anything here and step 1 of the protocol tells you to read it; this block is the status mirror rule §9.7 asks for, not a second copy. The full pre-iter128 mirror text is in tools/loop/gates-archive.json.

gates.gate-m2-aur-review: PENDING, MIRKO'S. The loop's half finished at iter113: 44 pages are up in DOCUMESBX. Needs your page-by-page review, then the tick. Caveat GATES.md states: cases/mermaid.md is deliberately absent (beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 rejects `graph TD;` and `pie`, and a page fails as a unit) - tick on the rendering you CAN see; the mermaid question is decisions.mermaidDialectGap, not this gate.
gates.gate-m3-approval-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the cheapest of the five: add ONE `approved` label to any published page ('CLI Reference', id 451969089, is a good one), then tick. The loop then runs `sync --labels`, republishes that page with `publish --notify-reviewers`, and you re-approve. `approvedBy` will read 'unknown' and that is correct, not a bug (spike S3: Confluence exposes no label author). THIS GATE ALSO GATES SHIPPED CODE - iter122's `--notify-reviewers` fires only where a run revokes an approval, and no DOCUMESBX page carries one, so nothing can exercise it live until this box moves.
gates.gate-m4-feedback-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S. Write ONE comment saying something factually wrong about a published page (an INLINE comment on a sentence exercises the most code), then tick. The loop then runs `sync --comments` -> `/docs-feedback` -> a `docs/feedback-<date>` PR -> republish -> `sync --reply`.
gates.gate-m5-refresh-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and it is a DECISION not a task: does M5's §14 acceptance run on this repo (copy docs-drift-pr.yml in, add secrets) or fold into M7 where a real repo with real PRs exists? Answer in decisions.m5Acceptance. The live middle of the chain is already done and re-runnable (iter121: `drift --mark` labelled 9 of 11 sourced pages against DOCUMESBX and proved a label spends no page version).
gates.gate-m6-first-release: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the only irreversible one - a package on a GitHub Packages feed cannot be unpublished, which is why the loop will not do it. Steps: (1) confirm Directory.Build.props <Version>, plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version and plugin/README.md's git-subdir ref all read the number you want (all three read 0.1.0; release.yml's first step refuses a mismatch before building, so a wrong guess costs nothing); (2) `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`; (3) delete the 'Not published yet' note from README.md; (4) tick. The loop then walks the README literally in a fresh empty directory - that walk IS M6's acceptance. A PAT with read:packages in the loop environment is needed for the install half.
gates.paste-force-push-hook: PENDING, MIRKO'S, ONE PASTE, NOTHING WAITS ON IT. Replace tools/loop/loop-settings.json with the single fenced json block in tools/loop/loop-settings-paste.md. Closes a measured hole in rule §8.2's [ENFORCED] deny list: `git push <remote> <ref> --force` and `--force-with-lease` were both ALLOWED (the patterns match whole tokens from the start of the command). The fix is the already-committed PreToolUse hook tools/loop/hooks/deny-history-rewrite.py, 25/25 both directions. The loop cannot install it — Edit on its own settings file is refused, and routing around that with python3 is exactly what the guard prevents. See the blockers array for the full question. PROVEN WORKING BEFORE INSTALL (iter131): the exact block, handed to a child session as a scratch settings file, refused the force push while the live settings let it reach git and a benign `git status` ran clean — 3/3, .mtk/paths-131/probe-hook-from-settings.py. So hooks DO load and fire from a --settings file; that question is no longer open.
gates.settings-corrections: PENDING, MIRKO'S, TWO ONE-LINERS, NOTHING WAITS ON EITHER. (a) This workspace is untrusted (~/.claude.json hasTrustDialogAccepted:false), so three `.claude/settings.json` allow entries — the `dotnet build/test/format` ones — are ignored every iteration; zero cost today because --settings supplies the broader `Bash(dotnet:*)`. (b) `Write(.env)` and `Write(.env.*)` in your GLOBAL settings enforce nothing: only `Edit(path)` rules are matched for file permissions. Full text in GATES.md.
gates.paste-format-on-edit-hook: PENDING, MIRKO'S, ONE PASTE, NOTHING WAITS ON IT. `.claude/settings.json`'s format-on-edit hook has fired and FAILED on every edit since the 2026-07-24 bootstrap (`$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is empty in a project settings file → `bash "/hooks/format-on-edit.sh"` → exit 127; the script was never generated). Invisible for 133 iterations because a failing PostToolUse hook never reaches the agent. Hooks are NOT gated by the untrusted workspace — that gates `permissions.allow` only, which closes iter131's lead. Paste tools/loop/claude-settings-paste.md's fenced block over that file, or answer "delete" in decisions.formatOnEditHook. Fix committed and tested 5/5, paste validated 12/12, proven end to end 3/3. Full instructions in GATES.md.

decisions._archive: FULL DECISION BODIES ARE IN tools/loop/decisions-archive.json, moved there at iter130 because this field was 11.6 KB of the 50 KB that put step 1's Read past its budget. NOTHING WAS DISCARDED and the round-trip was asserted before this file was rewritten (the seventh precedent, after doneArchive, blockersArchive, gatesArchive, methodNotes, scratchInventory and spikesArchive). Each key below is a one-line summary: what the decision is, whose call it is, and what to strike off which test when it is settled. `nextAction` carries the same list in the order worth settling, so orientation costs no extra Read; open the archive only to ACT on one. MIRKO: write your answer straight over the stub in this file — the key is what matters, not the text it replaces.
decisions.mermaidDialectGap: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter113. beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 renders `flowchart LR` + `sequenceDiagram`, REJECTS `graph TD;` (the trailing semicolon alone) and `pie`. decisions.m5Acceptance: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter121. Where M5's §14 acceptance runs: (a) install docs-drift-pr.yml here and open one PR (no secrets needed), (b) add secrets + docs-refresh/docs-publish, which makes every push to main publish to the sandbox, or (c) fold into M7 and reword §14. decisions.pushPolicy: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter121. May the loop `git push origin main`? Answer "always", "on-request" or "never". origin/main is at 699c855 ("iter74"); local main is [ahead 107] at iter130. Blocks the remote half of gate-m5 and makes gate-m6's tag step misleading. NOTE iter130: the day the loop may push is the day the force-push hole in blockers/paste-force-push-hook stops being theoretical. Full body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json and the blockers array.
decisions.planSection6Deviations: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter122. §6's preamble declares three global options that did not ship as declared: `--verbose` built NOWHERE, `--json` built on `status` alone (`drift` spells it `--format`), `--config` absent from `init`/`convert`. Either BUILD them (three slices) or CORRECT §6. Then strike the entry off `UnbuiltOptions` in tests/DocuMe.Core.Tests/Acceptance/PlanCommandSpecTests.cs. Full body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json.
decisions.planSection5Deviations: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter123. Two config fields load, validate, round-trip and are read by NO line of src/: `links.repoBlobUrl` (§6.2 step 2 specifies the behaviour and plugin/skills/docs-loop/SKILL.md:169 tells the skill it works) and `drift.defaultBranch`. Build or delete each. Then strike off `DeadFields` in PlanDataContractTests.cs AND delete the bullet from docs/wiki/20-reference/configuration.md's inert section — the test fails from both sides. Settle with planSection10Deviations (a). Full body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json.
decisions.planSection9Deviation: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter124. PLAN.md §9's CI-posture bullet and rule §1.5 both say feedback runs with "read-only repo access", which no job that opens a PR can have; docs-feedback.yml correctly grants contents: write, and docs/wiki/30-automation/workflows.md already words it right. Reword the plan and the rule to match. PLAN.md §9 the loop CAN edit; .claude/rules/security.md §1.5 IT CANNOT (needs your paste). Then strike off `PlanDeviations` in PlanSemanticsTraceTests.cs. Full body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json.

They are OBJECT-shaped entries carrying `{"iteration": NNN, "slice": …}` rather than a leading `iterNNN` string, so the string search that produced the lead could not see them. Measured across all 136 lines: 107 string entries, 29 object entries, **every iteration 1..135 present**, one legitimate duplicate (iter48 logged two slices).
(2) THE BIGGER FINDING, WHICH THE LEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE: `grep -n 'iterNNN' done-archive.jsonl` — the exact command `doneArchive.howToRead` prescribed — IS WRONG FOR 27 OF 135 ITERATIONS. It returns NOTHING for 3 (the object-shaped ones) and, for 24 more, returns ONLY lines belonging to some OTHER entry. That second half is the dangerous one because it looks like a hit: ask it for iter113 and it hands back lines 135 and 136 — iter134's and iter135's records, which cite iter113 in prose. Loop entries reference each other constantly, so 65 of 135 iterations get at least one match that is not their own record. Measured one iteration at a time against the lines that genuinely own each: .mtk/paths-136/probe-archive-lookup.py.
(3) `n` IS A LINE INDEX, NOT AN ITERATION NUMBER, and has not matched one since line 50: iter48's second entry offsets every later line by exactly +1 (87 of 136). `doneCount` 136 against iteration 135 is that offset, not a miscount. Recorded so nobody 'repairs' it by renumbering.
(4) LEAD (v) WAS PARTLY STALE and is corrected rather than repeated: iter133 DID add archive checks to check-state-size.py. But they are all checks over the FILE — valid JSON, contiguous `n`, matching `doneCount`, `doneRecent` round-trip — and a file satisfies every one of them while missing an iteration outright. Delete a middle record, renumber, and iter133's checks all pass.
(5) FIXED, in the script `readMe` already requires after every state.json edit rather than a new one nobody would remember to run: three checks stated in the archive's own domain — ATTRIBUTION (every entry names its iteration, in either shape), COVERAGE (no gap in the range), HEAD (the newest entry is the iteration state.json claims to be on). The head check is the one that would have caught iter132's loss at the moment it happened. Plus `--find <n>`, the lookup that actually works: it resolves both shapes and lists prose mentions SEPARATELY instead of returning them as answers.
(6) PROVEN GATES RATHER THAN DECORATION: .mtk/paths-136/mutate-archive-checks.py, **6/6**, each case building a scratch repo and asserting WHICH message fired. Two cases carry the non-redundancy proof — deleting a mid-history record (renumbered) and losing the newest record (doneRecent trimmed to match) both leave every pre-iter136 check GREEN, so only the new one fires. Two cases must STAY green: the unmutated control, and one iteration logged twice, because iter48's duplicate is legitimate. First run scored 4/6 and both misses were the HARNESS's prediction — stripping attribution also opens a coverage gap, so two checks correctly fire on one mutation; same shape as iter135's 6/7.
(7) PROSE CORRECTED WHERE IT WAS WRONG: `doneArchive.howToRead` no longer prescribes the broken grep, `format` names both shapes, and `howToAppend` says `n` is a line index.

doneArchive.format: JSONL, one {"n": <1-based LINE index>, "entry": <string|object>} per line, oldest first. **BOTH ENTRY SHAPES ARE LIVE and any reader must handle both** (counted iter136): 108 strings naming themselves in a leading `iterNNN`, 29 objects carrying `{"iteration": NNN, ...}`. **`n` IS NOT THE ITERATION NUMBER** - see howToAppend.

Split at iter127. NOTHING WAS DISCARDED - the archive holds every entry verbatim and the migration asserted the round-trip before rewriting this file.
doneArchive.howToRead: This is history, not orientation - do not read it whole. **USE `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py --find <iteration>`, NOT `grep`.** Measured at iter136 over all 135 iterations, a bare `grep -n 'iterNNN'` is WRONG FOR 27 OF THEM: nothing at all for the object-shaped entries, and for 24 more only lines belonging to some OTHER entry that cites that iteration in prose - which looks exactly like a hit. `--find` resolves both entry shapes and lists prose mentions separately. Forensics: method-notes.md, 'Reading the loop's own history back'. For a range, Read with offset/limit (one entry per line); `tail -3` still works.
doneArchive.howToAppend: EVERY ITERATION: append one line to the archive with n = doneCount + 1, bump doneCount, then set doneRecent to that SINGLE newest entry, verbatim. It was 5 until iter128 (which measured 8.5 KB in five entries against a state file that had to shed 27 KB), then 3, then 2; iter129 took it to 1 when the budget check tripped on its own prose and two long entries no longer fit. THE PATTERN IS THE POINT: the iteration that grows this file pays it back, rather than raising the budget to suit itself. ASSERT THE ENTRY YOU DROP IS ALREADY IN THE ARCHIVE before dropping it, and run `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` afterwards. THE ARCHIVE IS AUTHORITATIVE AND COMPLETE; doneRecent is a convenience tail and nothing more. If a condensed entry is what fits inline, condense it in BOTH places so the duplication stays verbatim. **`n` IS A LINE INDEX, NOT AN ITERATION NUMBER** (iter136): iter48 logged twice, so `n = iteration + 1` from n=50 on. Do NOT 'repair' that by renumbering. check-state-size.py now also checks ATTRIBUTION, COVERAGE and HEAD - the last would have caught iter132's loss when it happened.
